comparison: Both evaluate library design and experimental methodology (C65-C77, C7, C78-C83). OpenEval and peer reviewers agree the library construction is well-designed with appropriate controls and validation. Both find the approach SUPPORTED with high praise for experimental rigor.

OpenEval R2 focuses on assay validation (C7, C67, C78-C83) which overlaps with peer R1's evaluation of experimental design. Both agree the methodology is sound with strong validation through replicate correlations and control behavior. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate domain-level mutability patterns (C84-C86, C158, C161-C163, C169-C170). OpenEval and peer reviewers agree these structural-functional findings are well-supported by heatmap data and consistent with prior structural knowledge. Both find claims SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate beneficial mutations in origin-binding domain (C89-C96, C101-C102, C173-C175). OpenEval and peer reviewers agree these are key findings supported by structural mapping and comparison to natural sequences. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED with explicit endorsement as valuable contributions.

Both evaluate comparison to natural diversity (C117-C121, C145). OpenEval finds the quantitative findings well-supported. Peer reviewers accepted the finding that beneficial variants are absent in nature and the explanation regarding different selective pressures. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate validation experiments (C122-C127, C131-C134). OpenEval emphasizes correlation between assays and mechanistic insights. Peer reviewers explicitly validated the transduction data as important for gene therapy relevance. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

OpenEval R6 includes A213V promoter vs amino acid distinction (C129-C130) which peer R10 evaluates separately. Both accept the mechanistic interpretation with supporting data. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate S110R variant characterization (C131-C134, C178-C179). OpenEval notes findings supported by multiple assays with mechanism requiring further investigation. Peer reviewers validated these findings without challenge. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate cross-serotype consistency (C10-C11, C135-C137). Perfect claim overlap. OpenEval and peer reviewers agree this is a surprising and important finding with strong validation. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED with explicit praise.

Both evaluate nucleotide-level effects (C112-C115, C182-C187). OpenEval finds the c.849C>G effect statistically supported but mechanism unclear. Peer reviewers raised concerns about synonymous mutation assumptions and suggested examining mRNA levels. OpenEval is SUPPORTED while peer evaluation is UNCERTAIN due to incomplete understanding.

Both evaluate synonymous variants (C109-C110, C188-C189). OpenEval acknowledges assay limitations for detecting synonymous effects. Peer reviewers questioned the neutrality assumption and suggested additional analyses. OpenEval is SUPPORTED while peer evaluation is UNCERTAIN.

Both address limitations in detecting synonymous variant effects (C190-C192). OpenEval acknowledges these as appropriate limitations. Peer reviewers identify this as an area requiring further investigation. OpenEval is SUPPORTED while peer evaluation is UNCERTAIN.
Both evaluate zinc-finger domain mutability (C165-C170). OpenEval and peer reviewers agree the domain is dispensable, consistent with prior work. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED without challenge.

Both evaluate library format comparison (C87-C88). Perfect claim overlap. OpenEval and peer reviewers agree the correlation validates the approach and differential effects are expected. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

OpenEval R13 evaluates structural patterns in mutability (C103-C106) with minimal overlap to peer R3. Both accept structural mapping findings as supported by prior knowledge. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate interpretation of fitness value range and mutational constraints (C138-C144). Perfect claim overlap. OpenEval and peer reviewers agree the biological reasoning is sound and appropriately supported. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both address why beneficial variants are not found in nature (C146-C157). OpenEval finds the reasoning about lytic vs latent cycle constraints biologically sound. Peer reviewers initially requested discussion of this point, then accepted the authors' explanation. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

OpenEval R16 synthesizes findings about origin-binding domain (C171-C172, C176-C177, C181) with minimal overlap to peer R3. Both accept the clustering of beneficial mutations in this domain as a key finding. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

OpenEval R17 evaluates background and rationale claims (C1-C6, C12, C56-C64, C66). No corresponding peer review evaluation found. OpenEval finds these appropriately cited and logically structured as SUPPORTED.
OpenEval R18 evaluates detailed AAV biology background (C13-C55). No corresponding peer review evaluation found. OpenEval finds all claims appropriately cited to prior work as SUPPORTED.
OpenEval R19 evaluates summary claims about study accomplishments (C196-C198). No corresponding peer review evaluation found. OpenEval finds these well-supported by collective evidence as SUPPORTED.
